http.prompt: Explain how Aspire service references help an AI application. Evidence run 20260923-110938.

first.answer: Aspire service references facilitate the connection between AI applications by providing essential connection information. They ensure a consuming service only starts after the required dependencies report as ready or healthy, which is vital for maintaining a robust system. By doing so, it ensures the AI application can rely on other services being operational before it commences, which is crucial for consistent and accurate AI behavior [2].

sources.title: Built-in observability
sources.content: Aspire service defaults emit logs, metrics, and distributed traces through OpenTelemetry and display them in the Aspire dashboard.

sources.title: Service references
sources.content: WithReference passes connection information to a consuming service. WaitFor delays startup until a dependency reports ready or healthy.

sources.title: Caching
sources.content: Redis can cache repeated responses and shared application state, but cache keys must account for the prompt, model, and grounding context.

browser.prompt: Why should an Aspire AI application use health checks? Evidence run 20260923-110938.
browser.freshAnswer: An Aspire AI application should use health checks to ensure reliable operation and prompt issue detection, as it allows for continuous monitoring of the service's health and performance [3]. Additionally, health checks can aid in proactive problem resolution and maintain consistent user experience by detecting and alerting on potential issues before they impact end-users [3]. Note: This response is based on general best practices for AI application management and may not directly apply to the specific context of the Aspire service mentioned.
